tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on the Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text. v2 = (a) productize the M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)'; (b) callout-vs-room filtering.

prep.what: Add an AI-powered 'read labels' option for firms with outlined text (M3 tile vision), plus filter noise like arrows, callouts, and paragraph notes from room-name results.
prep.understand: PDFTron-outlined firms encode text as graphics — the live-text lane finds nothing on them. M3 tiling sends small PNG tiles to a vision model to OCR them. Without callout filtering, general-note paragraphs, 'UP' stair arrows, and 'FEC' callouts all match as room names (the R13 documented noise).
approach: Productize `run_labels_m3tiles.py` into the engine as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action gated behind the §7a metered-credits event.
Confirm the secrets approach for wiring MINIMAX_AI key to the VPS (`/opt/takeoff-engine/.env`).
Add callout-vs-room filter: reject strings matching paragraph/directional/callout patterns before they become room-name candidates.
Test on Harborview (currently 0 named → expect improvement) and Holabird regression (should stay ≥92/109 named).

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite scaffolded in B1. Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar between here and estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Expand the assembly engine from its scaffolded 'lite' state to produce real trade quantities — paint SF, drywall SF, floor SF, LF trim, ceiling SF — by classification and wall height.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` exists but generates placeholder quantities. The core missing link: `wall_area = perimeter × height`. Plans don't carry wall height, so you need a project-level default (suggest 9 ft) plus optional per-room override. Once wall SF is derivable, one classification maps to up to 8 estimator-grade lines.
approach: Define the assembly spec map: `room_type → [{quantity_type, formula, unit, csi_code}]` covering Bedroom, Bath, Kitchen, Corridor for CT Pros core trades.
Implement `wall_area = perimeter × height` in `engine/assemblies.py` using `geometry.rings` (perimeter already persisted by the canvas work).
Extend the Excel export to add an Assembly quantities tab showing per-room breakdown.
Validate on a test sheet: e.g. 12×12 room at 9 ft → 48 LF perimeter → 432 SF walls → cross-check against estimator intuition.
resources: CSI MasterFormat Div 09 (Finishes) reference for unit quantities
AZ Takeoff PRD Phase 1 assemblies section

tasks.title: Door recall round 2 + bi-fold / cased-opening recall
tasks.notes: Door recall is THE bottleneck blocking global SEAL_FT retirement. Localseal guard (t15) made chords safe. Push recall via raster-gap detection. Target >0.6 coverage on lagging sheets.

prep.what: Improve door/opening recall using raster-gap detection to raise chord coverage above 0.6 on the 4 sheets currently at 0.00, unblocking the global SEAL_FT retirement.
prep.understand: t15 (localseal guard) made additional chords safe — a bad chord now self-reverts. The bottleneck is coverage: 0.00 on holabird/mitchell/washington/merrimack; 0.32 dental; 0.64 brook_p4. Symbol-based detectors already failed on furniture noise. Raster-gap detection (finding breaks in wall-layer pixels) is the path forward.
approach: Survey the 4 zero-coverage sheets: identify which opening types are being missed (beyond bi-folds, which already ship).
Implement raster-gap detection: scan the wall-layer raster for pixel gaps narrower than SEAL_FT between two wall segments.
Baseline with `docs/spike/w13_localseal_guard.py` before the change, then rerun after to measure coverage gain — targeting >0.6 on ≥2 lagging sheets.
Gate on full 81-check gauntlet before committing.
resources: GT corpus (12 judges / 352 rooms) for per-sheet IoU verification

tasks.title: Sandbox-validate full QB round-trip against live Intuit
tasks.notes: All 6 QB entity mappings are mock-tested only. Run connect→estimate→invoice→paid against real sandbox. Document validation artifact in docs/.

prep.what: Run the complete QB connect→estimate→invoice→payment flow against the real Intuit sandbox and record a validation artifact proving the end-to-end works.
prep.understand: Every single QB entity sync in this codebase is mock-tested only — not a single real Intuit API call has been made in QA. Sandbox validation catches payload shape errors and edge cases (duplicate customer DisplayName 6240, LinkedTxn binding) that mocks cannot reveal. This is a hard go-live gate.
approach: Set `QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox` in .env, then OAuth-connect to a sandbox QBO company at developer.intuit.com.
Push the full flow: create Lead → approve estimate → `QBEstimateSync::push` → create invoice → `QBInvoiceSync::push` (verify IPPLinkedTxn links back to estimate).
Simulate payment in the QB sandbox UI, then run `php artisan quickbooks:sync` and verify `QBPaymentSyncer` records the delta in CRM.
Re-run the push twice (upsert idempotency) and commit a `docs/validation/qb-round-trip-sandbox-YYYYMMDD.md` artifact.
resources: QB OAuth App credentials (Google Cloud Console / Intuit Developer dashboard)

tasks.title: Sandbox-validate QBVendorSync (Subcontractor→Vendor) live
tasks.notes: QBVendorSync is the only QB entity never tested against real Intuit. Validate Subcontractor→Vendor push including adopt-by-DisplayName and 6240 duplicate recovery.

prep.what: Validate the Subcontractor→QB Vendor push against real Intuit sandbox, specifically proving the 6240 duplicate-DisplayName adopt-by-DisplayName recovery path and the Vendor1099 flag work.
prep.understand: QBVendorSync is the only entity that has NEVER been touched by a real Intuit call — not even in sandbox. The 6240 adopt path (if a Vendor with the same DisplayName exists, adopt it rather than create a duplicate) is critical for real-world use and is entirely unproven outside mocks.
approach: Create a test Subcontractor in the app (with W9 on file) and push to sandbox → verify Vendor created with Vendor1099=true.
Force the 6240 path: manually create a Vendor in the QB sandbox with the same DisplayName first, then re-push — verify adopt-by-DisplayName fires instead of erroring.
Push a sub without W9 on file → verify Vendor1099=false.
Document results in `docs/validation/`.
resources: Intuit QB API Vendor object docs (DisplayName uniqueness, Vendor1099 field)
QB sandbox UI for manual Vendor creation to force the 6240 path
